title.en: Volume 54 Treatises 35: Selection of Officials 4 - Ministry Selection, Provincial Selection, Honest Inspectors, Recommendations, Compensation for Achievements and Perpetual Faults
title.raw: 卷五十四 志第三十五: 選舉四 部選 省選 廉察 薦舉 功酬虧永 Volume 54 Treatises 35: Selection of Officials 4 - Ministry Selection, Provincial Selection, Honest Inspectors, Recommendations, Compensation for Achievements and Perpetual Faults

sentences.zh: 凡吏部選授之制，自太宗天會十二年，始法古立官，至天眷元年，頒新官制。

translations.literal: As for the Ministry of Personnel's system of selection and appointment, from Emperor Taizong's twelfth year of Tianhui it began to model antiquity in establishing offices, and by the first year of Tianjuan a new official system was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel's selection and appointment system began when Emperor Taizong, in Tianhui 12 (1134), restored offices on ancient models; by Tianjuan 1 (1138) a new official structure was issued.

sentences.zh: 及天德四年，始以河南、北選人並赴中京，吏部各置局銓注。

translations.literal: By the fourth year of Tiande, candidates from Henan and Hebei were first gathered together at the Central Capital, and the Ministry of Personnel established separate bureaus to review and register appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 4 (1156) candidates from the Henan and Hebei circuits were first required to report together at Zhongjing, where the Ministry of Personnel set up separate bureaus for certification and registration.

sentences.zh: 又命吏部尚書蕭賾定河南、北官通注格，以諸司橫班大解、並大將軍合注差人，依年例一就銓注，餘求仕人分四季擬授，遂為定制。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel Director Xiao Ze was also ordered to fix the general registration regulations for Henan and Hebei offices; persons with horizontal-rank grand release from various agencies and grand generals eligible for joint registration were all reviewed and registered at once according to annual precedent, while remaining office-seekers received draft appointments in four seasons—this became the standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Xiao Ze was also ordered to set unified registration rules for the Henan and Hebei circuits. Holders of horizontal-rank grand release from various agencies and eligible grand generals were certified in one annual batch; other office-seekers received seasonal draft appointments, and this became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，命擬注時，依舊令，求仕官明數謂面授也，不許就本鄉，若衰病年老者毋授繁劇處。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, when drafting nominations it was ordered that under the old statutes office-seekers must state their numbers—meaning face-to-face appointment—and were not permitted to take posts in their home districts; if feeble, ill, or elderly, they were not to be given demanding posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 (1154), draft nominations were again governed by the old rule that candidates declare their numbers for in-person assignment and could not take posts in their home districts; the frail, sick, or elderly were barred from demanding assignments.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定元年，敕從八品以下除授，不須奏聞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, it was decreed that appointments from the secondary eighth rank downward need not be reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 1 (1161), Emperor Shizong decreed that appointments from the secondary eighth rank down no longer required imperial report.

sentences.zh: 又制，求仕官毋入權門，違者追一官降除，有所饋獻而受之者，奏之。

translations.literal: It was also regulated that office-seekers must not enter the gates of powerful families; violators had one rank stripped and were demoted, and those who received gifts were reported.
translations.idiomatic: A further rule barred office-seekers from patronizing powerful households; violators lost one rank and were demoted, and any official who accepted gifts was reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔隨季選人，如無過或有功酬者，依格銓注。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict [stated that] seasonal candidates, if without fault or with merit compensation, were to be reviewed and registered according to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, seasonal candidates without fault or with merit compensation were to be certified under the standard regulations.

sentences.zh: 有廉能及汙濫者，約量升降，呈省。

translations.literal: Those with integrity and ability or with corruption and abuse were approximately promoted or demoted and submitted to the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: The honest and capable were promoted and the corrupt were demoted as appropriate, with reports sent to the provincial office.

sentences.zh: 七年，命有司，自今每季求仕人到部，令本部體問，政跡出眾者，及贓汙者，申省核實以聞，約量升擢懲斷，年老者勿授縣令。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the responsible offices were ordered that from now on each season when office-seekers arrived at the ministry, their home departments should investigate them; those with outstanding administrative records and those guilty of embezzlement were to be reported to the provincial office for verification, with approximate promotion, advancement, or punishment; the elderly were not to be given county magistracies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, each season's office-seekers were to be vetted by their home departments when they reached the ministry; outstanding performers and the corrupt were reported to the provincial office for verification and appropriate promotion or punishment, and the elderly were not appointed county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 又謂宰臣曰：「隨朝官能否，大率可知。

translations.literal: He also told the chief ministers: "For capital-attached officials, competence or incompetence can largely be known.
translations.idiomatic: He also told the chief ministers, "For officials attached to the capital, competence is usually plain to see.

sentences.zh: 若外路轉運司幕官以至縣令，但驗資考，其中縱有忠勤廉潔者，無路而進，是此人終身不敢望三品矣，豈進賢退不肖之道哉！

translations.literal: But for outer-circuit transport commissioners' staff members down to county magistrates, only seniority is checked; even if among them there are loyal, diligent, honest, and clean men, they have no path to advance—such a person would not dare hope for the third rank in a lifetime. How is this the way to advance the worthy and retire the unworthy!
translations.idiomatic: But for staff of outer-circuit transport commissions down to county magistrates, only seniority counts. Even the loyal, diligent, and incorrupt among them have no avenue of advancement and may never reach the third rank in a lifetime. How is that advancing the worthy and removing the unfit?

sentences.zh: 自今通三考視其能否，以定升降為格。

translations.literal: From now on, after three performance reviews assess their competence, use that to fix promotion and demotion as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, after three performance reviews, competence should determine promotion and demotion.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「今用人之法甚弊，其有不求聞達者，人仕雖久，不離小官，至三四十年不離七品者。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Today's method of employing men is very defective. Those who do not seek fame and advancement may serve long yet never leave minor posts—some for thirty or forty years never leave the seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Today's appointments are badly flawed. Men who do not court influence may serve for decades without leaving minor posts—some stay at the seventh rank for thirty or forty years.

sentences.zh: 而新進者結朝貴，致顯達，此豈示激勸之道。

translations.literal: Yet newcomers attach themselves to court grandees and reach eminence—how is this showing the way of encouragement and exhortation?
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile newcomers attach themselves to court grandees and rise to eminence. How does that encourage merit?

sentences.zh: 卿等當審於用人，以革此弊。

translations.literal: You must be careful in employing men to reform this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: You must be more careful in appointments and reform this abuse.

sentences.zh: 」時清州防禦使常德輝上言：「吏部格法，止敘年勞，是以雖有才能，拘於法而不得升，以致人材多滯下位。

translations.literal: " At that time Qingzhou Defense Commissioner Chang Dehui submitted: "The Ministry of Personnel regulations only count years of service, so that even when there is ability, one is bound by the law and cannot be promoted, causing talent to stagnate in lower positions.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Qingzhou Defense Commissioner Chang Dehui memorialized, "Ministry regulations count only years of service, so capable men are trapped by the rules and cannot advance, and talent piles up in the lower ranks.

sentences.zh: 又刺史縣令親民之職，多不得人，乞加體察，然後公行廉問，庶使有懼心。

translations.literal: Moreover, the posts of prefect and county magistrate, which deal closely with the people, often do not get the right men. I beg that investigation be increased, and then honest inspection be carried out openly, so that they may have a sense of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates, who work directly with the people, are often poorly chosen. I ask for closer scrutiny and open honest inspection so that officials will fear misconduct.

sentences.zh: 且今酒稅使尚選能者，況承流宣化之官，可不擇乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, today even wine-tax commissioners still select capable men—how much more for officials who carry out policy and transform the people—can they not be chosen?
translations.idiomatic: Even wine-tax commissioners are chosen for ability today—how much more should officials who carry policy to the people be carefully selected?

sentences.zh: 自今宜以能吏當任酒使者授親民之職。

translations.literal: From now on capable officials who would serve as wine commissioners should be given posts that deal with the people.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, capable officials who would qualify as wine-tax commissioners should be assigned to posts that serve the people directly.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The court] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，上謂宰臣曰：「守令以下小官，能否不能遍知。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the emperor told the chief ministers: "For minor officials such as prefects and magistrates and below, their competence cannot be known everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the emperor told his chief ministers, "It is impossible to know the competence of every minor official below the prefect and magistrate level.

sentences.zh: 比聞百姓或請留者，類皆不聽。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that when the common people sometimes petition to retain [an official], they are generally not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the people petition to keep a good official, their requests are usually ignored.

sentences.zh: 凡小官得民悅，上官多惡之，能承事上官者，必不得民悅。

translations.literal: Whenever minor officials win the people's approval, their superiors mostly dislike them; those who can serve their superiors' affairs inevitably fail to win the people's approval.
translations.idiomatic: Minor officials who please the people are often disliked by their superiors, while those who please their superiors rarely please the people.

sentences.zh: 自今民願留者，許直赴部，告呈省。

translations.literal: From now on, when the people wish to retain [an official], permit them to go directly to the ministry and report to the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, when the people wish to retain an official, let them report directly to the ministry and the provincial office.

sentences.zh: 遣使覆實，其績果善可超升之，如丞簿升縣令之類，以示激勸。

translations.literal: Send envoys to verify; if their achievements are truly good they may be promoted out of turn, as when a deputy or registrar is raised to county magistrate, to show encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to verify the record, and if it is genuinely good, promote the official out of turn—for example, raising a deputy or registrar to county magistrate—to encourage merit.

sentences.zh: 」二十六年，以闕官，敕：「見行格法合降資歷內，三降兩降各免一降，一降者勿降。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-sixth year, because of vacant posts, an edict [stated]: "Within the current regulations for seniority subject to demotion, for three demotions and two demotions each waive one demotion; for one demotion do not demote.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-sixth year, because offices stood vacant, an edict ruled that under current demotion rules, officials due for three or two demotions would each skip one step, and those due for one demotion would not be demoted.

sentences.zh: 省令譯史合得縣令資歷內，免錄事及下縣令各一任。

translations.literal: For provincial clerks and translator-scribes who qualify for county-magistrate seniority, waive one term each as registrar and as lower county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial clerks and translator-scribes who qualified for county-magistrate seniority were excused one term each as registrar and as lower-grade county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 密院令史三考以上者，同前免之。

translations.literal: Privy Council clerks with three performance reviews or more received the same waiver.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council clerks with three or more performance reviews received the same exemptions.

sentences.zh: 台、部、宗正府、統軍司令譯史，合曆縣令任數，免下令一任。

translations.literal: Censorate, ministry, Imperial Clan Court, and army command clerks and translator-scribes who had completed the required terms for county magistrate waived one term as lower magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and translator-scribes of the Censorate, ministries, Imperial Clan Court, and army commands who had served the requisite terms for county magistrate were excused one term as lower magistrate.

sentences.zh: 外路右職文資諸科，合曆縣令亦免一任。

translations.literal: Outer-circuit right-track civil candidates of various categories who had completed county-magistrate terms also waived one term.
translations.idiomatic: Outer-circuit right-track and civil-track candidates who had completed county-magistrate terms were also excused one term.

sentences.zh: 當過檢法知法，三考得錄事者，已後兩除一差。」

translations.literal: Those who had passed legal inspection and knowledge of law and after three reviews attained registrar—thereafter for every two appointments one was a substantive post."
translations.idiomatic: Those who had passed legal examinations and, after three reviews, reached registrar would thereafter receive one substantive appointment for every two nominations."

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，上曰：「舊制，每季到部求仕人，識字者試以書判，不識字者問以疑難三事，體察言行相副者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang, the emperor said: "Under the old system, office-seekers arriving at the ministry each season—those who could read were tested with documentary judgment; those who could not read were questioned on three difficult matters; conduct and words were investigated for consistency.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 3 (1192) the emperor said, "Under the old system, seasonal office-seekers at the ministry were tested on documentary judgment if literate and questioned on three difficult cases if not, with conduct matched against words.

sentences.zh: 其令自今隨季部人並令依條試驗。

translations.literal: Order that from now on all seasonal arrivals at the ministry be tested according to the articles.
translations.idiomatic: Order that from now on all seasonal candidates at the ministry be examined under those rules.

sentences.zh: 」宰執奏曰：「既體察知與所舉相同，又試中書判，若不量與升除，無以示勸。

translations.literal: " The chief executives reported: "Since investigation shows they match what was recommended and they also pass the documentary judgment test, if we do not promote them as appropriate, there is no way to show encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief executives replied, "If investigation confirms the recommendation and the candidate passes the judgment test, failure to promote appropriately would remove any incentive to excel.

sentences.zh: 」遂定制，若隨朝及外路六品以上官則隨長任用，外路正七品官擬升六品縣令一等除授，任滿合降者免降，從七品以下於各等資歷內減兩任擬注，以後體察相同即依已升任使，若體察不同者本等注授，若見任縣令升中上令者、並掌錢谷及丁憂去者，候解由到部。

translations.literal: " A standing rule was then fixed: capital-attached and outer-circuit officials of the sixth rank and above were appointed at the discretion of their superiors; outer-circuit proper seventh-rank officials were drafted for promotion one grade to sixth-rank county magistrate and appointed; those who on term completion should be demoted were exempted from demotion; from the secondary seventh rank downward, draft nominations within each seniority grade reduced two terms; thereafter if investigation matched, they were appointed according to the already advanced rank; if investigation differed, they received appointment at their original grade; if an incumbent county magistrate was promoted to upper-middle magistrate, or managed funds and grain, or left on mourning, they waited until their discharge certificate reached the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: " A standing rule followed: capital and outer-circuit officials of the sixth rank and above were appointed at their superiors' discretion; outer-circuit proper seventh-rank officials could be drafted one grade up to sixth-rank county magistrate, with demotion waived on term completion; from the secondary seventh rank down, draft nominations skipped two terms within each seniority grade; thereafter matching investigation allowed appointment at the advanced rank, while mismatched investigation meant appointment at the original grade; incumbent magistrates promoted to upper-middle magistrate, those managing revenue and grain, or those leaving for mourning waited until their discharge papers reached the ministry.

sentences.zh: 諸局分人亦候將來出職日准上擬注。

translations.literal: Personnel of various bureaus also waited until their future day of leaving clerical service to receive draft nominations as above.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau staff likewise waited until their scheduled departure from clerical service before receiving draft nominations under the same rules.

sentences.zh: 猛安謀克擬依前提刑司保舉到升任例，施行時嘗令隨門戶減一資歷。

translations.literal: Meng'an and mouke were to be drafted according to the earlier precedent of promotion through recommendation by the Punishments Bureau; when implemented they had once been ordered to reduce one seniority grade according to household.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'an and mouke units were to follow the earlier precedent of promotion through Punishments Bureau recommendation; when implemented, one seniority grade had been deducted by household.

sentences.zh: 明昌七年，敕複令如舊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Mingchang, an edict restored the order as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 7 (1196) an edict restored the earlier rule.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，上以縣令見守闕，近者十四月，遠者十六月，又以縣令丞簿員闕不相副，敕省臣：「右選官見格，散官至明威者注縣令，宣武者注丞簿，雖曾犯選格及虧永者亦注，是無別也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe, because county magistracies stood vacant awaiting incumbents—fourteen months in nearby circuits, sixteen in distant ones—and because the numbers of magistrates, deputies, and registrars did not match, the emperor ordered the provincial ministers: "Under the current regulations for right-track selection, those with honorary rank up to Mingwei are nominated as county magistrates and those with Xuanwu as deputies and registrars; even those who had violated selection regulations or had perpetual faults were also nominated—there is no distinction.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 (1201), with county magistracies vacant for fourteen months nearby and sixteen months in distant circuits, and magistrate, deputy, and registrar posts out of balance, the emperor told the provincial ministers, "Under current right-track rules, honorary ranks up to Mingwei qualify for county magistrate and Xuanwu for deputy and registrar—even men who had violated selection rules or carried perpetual faults were nominated the same way, with no distinction.

sentences.zh: 」遂定制，曾犯選格及虧永者，廣威注令，明威注丞簿。

translations.literal: " A standing rule was then fixed: those who had violated selection regulations or had perpetual faults were nominated as magistrates with Guangwei rank and as deputies and registrars with Mingwei rank.
translations.idiomatic: " A standing rule followed: men who had violated selection rules or carried perpetual faults were nominated as magistrates only at Guangwei rank and as deputies or registrars at Mingwei rank.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王大安元年，以縣令闕少，令初入上中下令者，與其守闕可令再注丞簿一任，俟員闕相副則當復舊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an under Emperor Weishao, because county magistracies were few in vacancies, those first entering upper-middle magistrate rank while holding a vacancy could be given one more term as deputy or registrar in draft nomination; when posts and vacancies matched they should return to the old rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an 1 (1209) under Emperor Weishao, because magistrate vacancies were scarce, newcomers to upper-middle magistrate who were holding a vacancy could be drafted for one more term as deputy or registrar; when posts and vacancies were again balanced, the old rule would apply.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐二年，以播越流離，官職多闕，權命河朔諸道宣撫司得擬七品以下，尋以所注吏部不知，季放之闕多至重複，乃奏罷之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou under Emperor Xuanzong, because of displacement and wandering, many offices stood vacant; it was provisionally ordered that the pacification commissions of the Hebei circuits might draft appointments for the seventh rank and below; soon because the appointments were unknown to the Ministry of Personnel, seasonal releases of vacancies often reached duplication, and memorial was made to abolish this.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 (1214) under Emperor Xuanzong, with the court displaced and offices widely vacant, pacification commissions on the Hebei frontier were temporarily allowed to draft appointments through the seventh rank; because the Ministry of Personnel was not informed, seasonal vacancy lists soon duplicated, and the arrangement was abolished on memorial.

sentences.zh: 時李英言：「兵興以來，百務煩冗，政在用人，舊雖有四善、十七最之法，而拔擢蔑聞，幾為徒設。

translations.literal: At that time Li Ying said: "Since warfare arose, the hundred affairs have been numerous and burdensome; governance lies in employing men. Although there were formerly the methods of four excellences and seventeen superlatives, promotion and advancement have scarcely been heard of—they have nearly become empty provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Ying said, "Since the wars began, affairs have multiplied and good government depends on appointing the right men. The old rules of four excellences and seventeen superlatives are barely used for promotion and have become nearly meaningless.

sentences.zh: 大定間，以監察御史及審錄官分詣諸路，考核以擬，號為得人，可依已試之效，庶幾使人自勵。

translations.literal: During Dading, censorial investigators and review-recording officials were sent separately to the various circuits to assess and draft nominations, acclaimed as obtaining the right men; one may rely on effects already tested, so that perhaps men will encourage themselves.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading era, censorial investigators and review officials toured the circuits to assess officials and draft nominations, with good results; that tested method should be revived so that men will strive to excel.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，戶部郎中奧屯阿虎言：「諸色遷官並與女直一體，而有司不奉，妄生分別，以至上下相疑。

translations.literal: In the third year, Households Bureau Director Aotun Ahu said: "Officials of all categories transferring posts are uniformly treated the same as Jurchens, yet the responsible offices do not comply and arbitrarily create distinctions, so that superiors and subordinates come to suspect one another.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Households Bureau Director Aotun Ahu said, "Officials of every background should be treated like Jurchens when transferring posts, but the responsible offices ignore this, invent distinctions, and breed mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 」詔以違制禁之。

translations.literal: " An edict forbade this as violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade the practice as a violation of regulations.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗之南遷也，詔吏部以秋冬于南京、春夏於中都置選，而赴調者憚於北行，率皆南來，遂並于南京設之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Xuanzong moved south, the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to hold selection in Nanjing in autumn and winter and at the Central Capital in spring and summer; but those reporting for assignment feared traveling north and mostly all came south, so selection was combined and established at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong moved south, the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to hold selection at Nanjing in autumn and winter and at Zhongdu in spring and summer; candidates feared traveling north and mostly reported to Nanjing, so selection was consolidated there.

sentences.zh: 三月，命汰不勝官者，令五品以上官公舉，今季赴部人內，先擇材幹者量緩急易之。

translations.literal: In the third month, incompetent officials were ordered eliminated; officials of the fifth rank and above were to recommend publicly; among those arriving at the ministry this season, first select capable men and exchange them according to urgency.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, incompetent officials were ordered removed; fifth-rank officials and above were to recommend replacements publicly; among this season's candidates at the ministry, capable men were to be chosen first and assigned according to urgency.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，詔有司議減冗員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding, the responsible offices were ordered to discuss reducing redundant personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 1 (1217) the responsible offices were ordered to discuss cutting redundant posts.

sentences.zh: 又詔，自今吏部每季銓選，差女直、漢人監察各一員監視，又盡罷前犯罪降除截罷、及承應未滿解去而複為隨處官司委使者。

translations.literal: Another edict [stated that] from now on at each season's selection and review by the Ministry of Personnel, one Jurchen and one Han inspector were to be dispatched to supervise; also completely abolish those previously demoted or dismissed for crimes, and attendants who left before completing their term yet again became agents commissioned by local offices everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict required that each seasonal ministry selection be supervised by one Jurchen and one Han inspector, and abolished officials previously demoted or dismissed for crimes, as well as attendants who left before completing their terms yet were again commissioned by local offices.

sentences.zh: 又定制，權依劇縣例俱作正七品，令隨朝七品、外路六品以上職事官，舉正七品以下職事官年未六十無公私罪堪任使者，歲一人，仍令兼領樞密院彈壓之職，以鎮軍人。

translations.literal: Another standing rule provisionally followed the precedent of demanding counties, all treated as proper seventh rank; capital-attached seventh-rank and outer-circuit sixth-rank and above functional officials were to recommend functional officials of the proper seventh rank and below, under sixty years of age, without public or private offenses, capable of service—one per year—who were also to hold concurrently the Privy Council post of suppressing disturbances, to restrain soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Another rule, following demanding-county precedent, treated the posts as proper seventh rank; capital seventh-rank and outer-circuit sixth-rank functional officials were to recommend proper seventh-rank and below officials under sixty without offenses, one per year, who would also hold Privy Council authority to suppress disturbances and control troops.

sentences.zh: 凡上司不得差占及淩辱決罰。

translations.literal: In general superiors might not requisition them or insult and punish them by decision.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors could not requisition them or insult and punish them arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 到任半年，委巡按官體訪具申籍記。

translations.literal: After half a year in office, touring inspectors were commissioned to investigate and report fully for registry.
translations.idiomatic: After six months in office, touring inspectors investigated and filed full reports for the registry.

sentences.zh: 又半年覆察，考滿日分等升用。

translations.literal: After another half year they were re-inspected; on completion of the review term they were promoted in graded use.
translations.idiomatic: After another six months they were reinspected, and at term's end were promoted by grade.

sentences.zh: 如六事備為上等，升職一等，四事為中等，減二資歷，其次下等減一資歷，不稱者截罷。

translations.literal: If all six matters were complete, upper grade—promote one rank in office; four matters, middle grade—reduce two seniority grades; next, lower grade—reduce one seniority grade; if unfit, dismiss outright.
translations.idiomatic: If all six criteria were met, upper grade meant promotion one rank; four criteria meant middle grade and reduction of two seniority steps; the next lower grade meant one seniority step down; the unfit were dismissed outright.

sentences.zh: 凡省選之制，自熙宗皇統八年以上京僻遠，始命詣燕京擬注，歲以為常。

translations.literal: As for the provincial selection system, from the eighth year of Huangtong under Emperor Xizong, because the upper capital was remote and secluded, it was first ordered to go to Yanjing for draft nominations, annually as the constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial selection system began in Huangtong 8 (1148) under Emperor Xizong, when officials from the remote upper capital were first required to travel to Yanjing for draft nominations each year.

sentences.zh: 貞元遷都，始罷是制。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved in Zhenyuan, this system was first abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved in the Zhenyuan era, this rule was abolished.

sentences.zh: 其常調製，正七品兩任升六品，六品三任升從五品，從五品兩任升正五品，正五品三任升刺史。

translations.literal: Its regular-transfer system: proper seventh rank, two terms to rise to sixth rank; sixth rank, three terms to rise to secondary fifth rank; secondary fifth rank, two terms to rise to proper fifth rank; proper fifth rank, three terms to rise to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Under the regular-transfer system, proper seventh rank advanced to sixth after two terms; sixth rank to secondary fifth after three; secondary fifth to proper fifth after two; proper fifth to prefect after three.

sentences.zh: 凡內外官皆以三十月為考，隨朝官以三十月為任，升職一等。

translations.literal: All inner and outer officials took thirty months as a performance review; capital-attached officials took thirty months as a term, promoting one rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: All inner and outer officials were reviewed every thirty months; capital-attached officials served thirty-month terms and advanced one rank on completion.

sentences.zh: 自非制授，尚書選在外官，命左司移文勾取。

translations.literal: Except for imperial appointment by decree, the Director selected outer officials; the Left Office was ordered to send documents to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: Except for imperial appointments, the Director selected outer officials and ordered the Left Office to summon them by document.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，始命置簿勾取。

translations.literal: In the third year of Cheng'an, registers for summoning were first ordered established.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 3 (1198) registers for summoning officials were first established.

sentences.zh: 大定十五年，制凡二品官及宰執樞密使不理任，每及三十月則書于貼黃，不及則附于闕滿簿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Dading, it was regulated that all second-rank officials and chief ministers and privy councilors did not count terms; every thirty months it was written on the yellow slip; if not reached, it was attached to the vacancy-completion register.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 15 (1175) it was ruled that second-rank officials, chief ministers, and privy councilors did not count formal terms; every thirty months this was noted on the yellow slip, or otherwise recorded on the vacancy register.

sentences.zh: 內外三品官以五十月為任。

translations.literal: Inner and outer third-rank officials took fifty months as a term.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer third-rank officials served fifty-month terms.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年，制凡文資右職官應遷三品職事者，五品以上曆五十月，六品以下及門廕雜流職事至四品以上而散官應至三品者，皆曆六十月，方許告遷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, it was regulated that all civil-track and right-track officials who should transfer to third-rank functional posts—fifth rank and above after fifty months; sixth rank and below and hereditary-entry miscellaneous streams with functional posts up to fourth rank and above while honorary rank should reach third rank—all after sixty months were permitted to petition for transfer.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 (1203) civil- and right-track officials eligible for third-rank functional posts needed fifty months of service from the fifth rank up, while sixth rank and below, hereditary entrants, and those with fourth-rank functional posts but third-rank honorary rank needed sixty months before petitioning for transfer.

sentences.zh: 七年，自按察使副依舊三十月理考外，內外四品以四十月理考，通八十月遷三品。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, except that surveillance commissioner deputies still processed reviews at thirty months as before, inner and outer fourth-rank officials processed reviews at forty months, totaling eighty months to transfer to third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, surveillance commissioner deputies still completed reviews in thirty months, but other inner and outer fourth-rank officials did so in forty months, for a total of eighty months before transfer to the third rank.

sentences.zh: 泰和八年，詔以門廕官職事至四品者甚少，自今至刺史而散官應至三品者，即許告遷三品。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taihe, an edict [stated that] because hereditary-entry officials reaching fourth-rank functional posts were very few, from now on those reaching prefect while honorary rank should reach third rank were permitted to petition for transfer to third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 8 (1208) an edict noted that few hereditary-entry officials reached fourth-rank functional posts; from then on those who reached prefect with honorary rank qualifying for the third rank could petition for third-rank transfer.

sentences.zh: 此省選資考之制也。

translations.literal: This was the provincial selection system of seniority and review.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the provincial selection system of seniority and performance review.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定元年，上謂宰臣曰：「朕昔曆外任，不能悉知人之優劣，每除一官必以不稱職為憂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, the emperor told the chief ministers: "I formerly served in outer posts and could not fully know men's excellence or inferiority; every time I appointed one official I was anxious he might be unfit.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 1 (1161) Emperor Shizong told his chief ministers, "When I served in the provinces I could not know every man's worth, and every appointment made me fear I had chosen someone unfit.

sentences.zh: 夫薦賢乃相職，卿等其各盡乃心，勿貽笑天下。

translations.literal: Recommending the worthy is the chancellor's duty—you must each give your full hearts and not bring laughter on the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Recommending worthy men is a chancellor's duty. Give your full effort and do not make the empire a laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「凡擬注之際當為官擇人，勿徒任親舊，庶無曠官矣。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Whenever drafting nominations, one should choose men for the office, not merely employ kin and old friends, so that perhaps there will be no vacant offices.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "When drafting nominations, choose men for the office, not merely kin and old friends, so that posts will not stand empty.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「守令之職當擇材能，比聞近邊殘破多用年老及罪降者，是益害邊民也。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The posts of prefect and magistrate should select for ability and talent. Recently I have heard that on the ravaged frontier they mostly use the elderly and those demoted for crimes—this only harms the frontier people more.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Prefects and magistrates should be chosen for ability. I hear the ravaged frontier is staffed with the elderly and men demoted for crimes, which only harms the border people further.

sentences.zh: 若資歷高者不當任邊遠，可取以下之才能者升授，回不復降，庶可以完複邊陲也。

translations.literal: If those with high seniority should not serve in remote border regions, take capable men from lower ranks and promote them, and on return do not demote them again—perhaps the frontier marches can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Men of high seniority should not serve on distant frontiers; promote capable men from lower ranks instead, and do not demote them on return, so that the borderlands may be restored.

sentences.zh: 」邊升之制，蓋始於此。

translations.literal: " The frontier-promotion system probably began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier-promotion system began here.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔監當官遷散官至三品尚任縣令者，與省除。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict [stated that] supervisory officials whose honorary rank had risen to third rank while still serving as county magistrates were to receive provincial dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, supervisory officials whose honorary rank had reached the third rank while still serving as county magistrates were to receive provincial appointments instead.

sentences.zh: 四年，敕隨朝六品以繁劇局分官有闕者，省不得擬注，令具闕及人以聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict [stated that] for capital-attached sixth rank and above, when demanding bureau posts had vacancies, the provincial office might not draft nominations but was to list vacancies and men and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when demanding bureau posts held by capital sixth-rank officials and above stood vacant, the provincial office could not draft nominations but had to report the vacancies and available men.

sentences.zh: 六年，制官至三品除，朝廷約量勞績歲月，特恩遷官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, it was regulated that when rank reached third rank for dismissal, the court approximately weighed merit and months of service for special-grace transfer in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when officials reached third rank for dismissal, the court weighed merit and length of service for special-grace promotion.

sentences.zh: 七年，制內外三品官遇擬注，其曆過成考以上月日，不曾遷加，或經革撥，可於除目內備書以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, it was regulated that when inner and outer third-rank officials encountered draft nomination, the months and days beyond completed performance reviews, without promotion or advancement, or having undergone reorganization, might be fully written in the appointment roster and reported.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when third-rank officials were drafted for nomination, months beyond completed reviews without promotion, or time after reorganization, were to be recorded fully in the appointment roster and reported.

sentences.zh: 又敕，外路四品以上職事官、並五品合升除官，皆具闕及人以聞。

translations.literal: Another edict [stated that] outer-circuit functional officials of the fourth rank and above and fifth-rank officials due for promotion or dismissal all listed vacancies and men and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict required outer-circuit fourth-rank functional officials and above, and fifth-rank officials due for promotion or dismissal, to report vacancies and candidates.

sentences.zh: 六品以下官，命尚書省擬定而複奏。

translations.literal: Officials of the sixth rank and below were ordered drafted by the provincial office and then memorialized again.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the sixth rank and below were drafted by the provincial office and then resubmitted for approval.

sentences.zh: 上又謂宰臣曰：「擬注外官，往往未當。

translations.literal: The emperor again told the chief ministers: "Draft nominations for outer officials are often inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again told his chief ministers, "Draft nominations for provincial officials are often inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 州縣之官良則政舉，否則政隳。

translations.literal: If prefectural and county officials are good, government is raised; if not, government collapses.
translations.idiomatic: Good prefectural and county officials raise government; bad ones ruin it.

sentences.zh: 卿宜辨論人材，優劣參用，則遞相勉勵，庶幾成治矣。

translations.literal: You should distinguish and discuss men's talents, employing excellent and inferior together, so that they encourage one another in turn—perhaps good governance can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: You should assess men's talents and employ the strong and weak together so they encourage one another, and good governance may be achieved.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「從來頓舍人例為節副，今宣徽院同簽銀術可以特收頓舍，然後授以滄州同知，此亦何功，但其人有足任使，故授以同簽也。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Formerly lodging attendants were routinely made military commissioners' deputies; now the Palace Attendant Office co-signer Yintu can specially receive lodging attendants and then be appointed Cangzhou Vice Commissioner—what merit is this? Yet the man is fully capable of service, so he was given co-signer.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Lodging attendants were usually made military commissioners' deputies. Now Palace Attendant Office co-signer Yintu was specially allowed to take lodging attendants and then appointed Cangzhou vice commissioner. What merit was that? Yet the man was capable, so he received the co-signer post.

sentences.zh: 且如自護衛、符寶、頓舍考滿者與六品五品之職，而與元苦辛特收頓舍者例除，則是不倫也。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who from the guard, talisman vault, and lodging attendants complete their reviews receive sixth- and fifth-rank posts, yet those who from the start suffered hardship in specially receiving lodging attendants receive routine dismissal—this is inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: Guards, talisman vault staff, and lodging attendants who complete their reviews receive fifth- and sixth-rank posts, while men who suffered hardship to become lodging attendants receive routine appointments—that is inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 」十年，謂宰臣曰：「凡在官者，若不為隨朝職任，便不能離常調。

translations.literal: " In the tenth year, he told the chief ministers: "For all who hold office, if they do not take capital-attached functional posts, they cannot leave the regular transfer track.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth year he told his chief ministers, "Officials who do not take capital functional posts cannot escape the regular transfer track.

sentences.zh: 若以卿等所知任使恐有滯，如驗入仕名項或廉等第用之亦可。

translations.literal: If employing men known to you fears stagnation, verifying entry records or integrity grades for use is also acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If relying only on men you know risks stagnation, you may also use entry records or integrity grades.

sentences.zh: 若不稱職，即與外除。

translations.literal: If unfit for office, then give outer dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: If they prove unfit, assign them to provincial posts instead.

sentences.zh: 」十一年，上謂宰臣曰：「隨朝官多自計所曆，一考謂當得某職，兩考又當得某職，故但務因循而已。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh year, the emperor told the chief ministers: "Capital-attached officials mostly calculate their own seniority—after one review they think they should get a certain post, after two reviews again a certain post—so they only attend to routine compliance.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh year the emperor told his chief ministers, "Capital officials mostly count their own seniority—after one review they expect a certain post, after two another—and therefore do only the minimum.

sentences.zh: 及被差遣，又多稽違。

translations.literal: When dispatched on missions, they mostly delay and disobey.
translations.idiomatic: When dispatched on missions, they often delay and disobey.

sentences.zh: 近除大理司直李寶為警巡使，而奏謝言'臣內曆兩考'，意謂合得五品則除六品也。

translations.literal: Recently Li Bao, Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, was appointed patrol commissioner, yet in his memorial of thanks he said 'I have two inner reviews,' meaning he thought he should get the fifth rank but was given the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Li Bao, Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, was appointed patrol commissioner, yet in his thanks he said, "I have completed two inner reviews," meaning he thought he deserved the fifth rank but received the sixth.

sentences.zh: 朕以此人幹事，嘗除監察御史，及為大理司直，未嘗言情見一事，由是除長官，欲視其為政，故授是職。

translations.literal: I regard this man as capable in affairs; he was once appointed censorial investigator, and as Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review he never once spoke of feelings or saw to a single matter; therefore I appointed him chief to observe his governance, and so gave this post.
translations.idiomatic: I consider him capable. He once served as censorial investigator, and as Direct Clerk he never once pressed personal claims or handled a case on his own. I appointed him chief to see how he would govern, and gave him this post for that reason.

sentences.zh: 自今外路與內除者，察其為政公勤則升用，若但務苟簡者，不必待任滿即當依本等出之。

translations.literal: From now on for outer-circuit and inner appointments, observe whether their governance is fair and diligent then promote; if they only attend to perfunctory simplicity, without waiting for term completion they should be released at their original grade.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, for provincial and capital appointments, promote those who govern fairly and diligently; those who merely coast need not wait for term's end but should be released at their original grade.

sentences.zh: 不明賞罰，何以示勸勉也。

translations.literal: If rewards and punishments are not clear, how can encouragement and exhortation be shown?
translations.idiomatic: Without clear rewards and punishments, how can we encourage merit?

sentences.zh: 」十二年，上謂宰臣曰：「朕嘗取尚書省百官行止觀之，應任刺史知軍者甚少，近獨深州同知辭不習為可，故用之。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth year, the emperor told the chief ministers: "I once took the conduct records of all officials of the provincial office to observe them; those fit to serve as prefect or army commander were very few. Recently only Shenzhou Vice Commissioner Ci Buxi was acceptable, so I used him.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth year the emperor told his chief ministers, "I once reviewed the conduct records of all provincial officials; few were fit for prefect or army command. Recently only Shenzhou Vice Commissioner Ci Buxi was acceptable, so I appointed him.

sentences.zh: 即今居五品者皆再任當例降之人，故不可也。

translations.literal: Those now holding the fifth rank are all men serving a second term who should by rule be demoted, so it is not possible.
translations.idiomatic: Those now at the fifth rank are all serving second terms and due for routine demotion, so they will not do.

sentences.zh: 護衛中有考滿者，若令出職，慮其年幼不閑政事，兼宿衛中如今日人材亦難得也。

translations.literal: Among the guards there are those who have completed reviews; if ordered to leave clerical service, I fear they are young and unfamiliar with government affairs, and moreover in the palace guard today talent is also hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Some guards have completed their reviews; if sent out to office, I fear they are young and unfamiliar with government, and talent in the palace guard is hard to find today.

sentences.zh: 若勒留承應，累其資考，令至正五品可乎？

translations.literal: If compelled to remain as attendants and their seniority and reviews accumulate, allowing them to reach proper fifth rank—would that do?
translations.idiomatic: If they were kept as attendants and their seniority accumulated until they reached the proper fifth rank, would that work?

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「善。

translations.literal: " All said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " All said, "Excellent.

sentences.zh: 」十六年，敕宰臣：「選調擬注之際，須引外路求仕人，引至尚書省堂量材受職。

translations.literal: " In the sixteenth year, the chief ministers were ordered: "At the time of selection, transfer, and draft nomination, outer-circuit office-seekers must be brought in and led to the provincial office hall to have their talents measured and receive posts.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixteenth year the chief ministers were ordered, "When selecting and drafting nominations, outer-circuit office-seekers must be brought to the provincial office hall to have their talents assessed and receive appointments.

sentences.zh: 」二十一年，謂宰臣曰：「海陵時，與人本官太濫，今複太隘，令散官小者奏之。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-first year, he told the chief ministers: "Under Emperor Hailing, granting men their original offices was too lax; now it is again too narrow—let those with small honorary rank be reported.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-first year he told his chief ministers, "Under Emperor Hailing, appointments to original offices were too loose; now they are too tight. Let men with lower honorary ranks be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」二十四年，以舊資考太滯，命各減一任，臨時量人材、辛苦、資歷、年甲，以次奏稟。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-fourth year, because old seniority and reviews were too stagnant, each was ordered reduced by one term; temporarily weighing talent, hardship, seniority, and age, report in order.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-fourth year, because old seniority rules were too rigid, each official's required terms were reduced by one; talent, hardship, seniority, and age were to be weighed case by case and reported in order.

sentences.zh: 章宗大定二十九年，定制，自正七品而上皆以兩任而後升。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading under Emperor Zhangzong, a standing rule was fixed: from the proper seventh rank upward all advanced after two terms.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 29 (1189) under Emperor Zhangzong, a rule fixed that all officials from the proper seventh rank up advanced only after two terms.

sentences.zh: 明昌四年，以前制有職官已帶三品者不許告遷，有司因之不舉，以致無由遷敘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Mingchang, because the former rule held that functional officials already bearing third rank were not permitted to petition for transfer, the responsible offices accordingly did not recommend them, so that there was no means of transfer and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 4 (1193), an old rule barred functional officials who already held third-rank honorary titles from petitioning for transfer; the responsible offices therefore stopped recommending them, leaving no path for advancement.

sentences.zh: 上慮其滯，遂定制，已帶三品散官寶曆五十月，從有司照勘，格前進官一階，格後為始再算。

translations.literal: The emperor feared this stagnation and fixed a rule: those already bearing third-rank honorary office, after fifty actual months, following the responsible offices' verification, advanced one rank step before the regulations and began counting anew from after the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing stagnation, the emperor fixed a rule: officials who already held third-rank honorary titles, after fifty actual months verified by the responsible offices, advanced one rank step under the old scale and began counting anew under the new scale.

sentences.zh: 五年，命宰臣擬注之際，召赴選人與之語，以觀其人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when chief ministers drafted nominations, candidates reporting for assignment were summoned to converse with them, to observe the men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when chief ministers drafted nominations, they were to summon candidates and speak with them to assess their character.

sentences.zh: 六年，命隨朝五品之要職，及外路三品官，皆具人闕進呈，以聽制授。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, important posts of capital fifth rank and outer-circuit third-rank officials were all to list men and vacancies and submit for imperial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, important capital fifth-rank posts and outer-circuit third-rank offices were to be submitted with lists of candidates and vacancies for imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 七年，敕隨朝除授必欲至三十月，如有急闕，則具闕及人奏稟。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict [stated that] capital appointments must reach thirty months; if there were urgent vacancies, list vacancies and men and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, an edict required capital appointments to run thirty months; urgent vacancies were to be reported with lists of candidates.

sentences.zh: 尋複令，不須待考滿後，當通算其所曆而已。

translations.literal: Soon it was ordered again that one need not wait until reviews were complete but should comprehensively calculate seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was ordered that officials need not wait for review completion but should have their total seniority calculated.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，敕宰臣曰：「凡除授，恐未盡當。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Cheng'an, the chief ministers were ordered: "For all appointments and dismissals, I fear they are not entirely appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 4 (1199) the chief ministers were ordered, "I fear our appointments are not always appropriate.

sentences.zh: 今無門下省，雖有給事中而無封駁司，若設之，使於擬奏未受時詳審得當，然後授之可也。

translations.literal: Now there is no Gate Department; although there are supervisory attendants there is no sealing-and-rebuttal office. If one were established, let it scrutinize draft memorials in detail before acceptance, and then appointment would be possible.
translations.idiomatic: There is no Gate Department now; although there are supervisory attendants, there is no office to seal and rebut memorials. If such an office were created to scrutinize draft nominations before approval, appointments would be more reliable.

sentences.zh: 」乃立審官院，凡所送令詳審者，以五日內奏或申省。

translations.literal: " The Review-of-Officials Office was then established; all orders sent for detailed review were to be memorialized or reported to the provincial office within five days.
translations.idiomatic: " The Review-of-Officials Office was established; all orders sent for detailed review were to be reported to the throne or the provincial office within five days.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，以六品、從五品闕少，敕命曆三任正七品而後升六品。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Cheng'an, because sixth-rank and secondary fifth-rank vacancies were few, it was decreed that after three terms as proper seventh rank one then rose to sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 5 (1200), because sixth-rank and secondary fifth-rank vacancies were scarce, officials were required to serve three terms at proper seventh rank before advancing to sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，諭旨宰臣曰：「凡遇急闕，與其用資歷未及之人，何如止起複丁憂舊人也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe, the chief ministers were instructed: "Whenever urgent vacancies arise, rather than using men whose seniority has not yet arrived, how about only recalling former officials who have left mourning?
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 (1201) the chief ministers were instructed, "When urgent vacancies arise, rather than appointing men whose seniority is insufficient, why not recall former officials who have completed mourning?

sentences.zh: 」命內外官通算，合得升等而少十五月者，依舊在職補足，而後升除，或有餘月日以後積算。

translations.literal: " Inner and outer officials were ordered to calculate comprehensively; those who qualified for promotion but lacked fifteen months were to complete them in their current posts, then be promoted or dismissed; surplus months and days were accumulated for later.
translations.idiomatic: " Inner and outer officials were to have seniority calculated comprehensively; those eligible for promotion but short by fifteen months would complete the time in their current posts before advancement; surplus months would count toward later promotion.

sentences.zh: 遇闕而無相應人，則以資歷近者奏稟。

translations.literal: When vacancies arose and there were no corresponding men, those nearest in seniority were reported.
translations.idiomatic: When vacancies arose with no fully qualified candidate, the nearest in seniority was reported.

sentences.zh: 二年，命少五月以下者本任補，六月至十四月者本任或別除補之。

translations.literal: In the second year, those short by five months or less were to complete in their current post; those short six to fourteen months were to complete in their current post or in another appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, those short by five months or less completed the time in their current post; those short six to fourteen months did so in their current post or another appointment.

sentences.zh: 是制既行之後，至六年，以一例遞升複恐太濫，命量材續稟。

translations.literal: After this system had been implemented, by the sixth year, because uniform stepwise promotion again feared being too lax, talent was to be weighed and reports continued.
translations.idiomatic: After this system had run six years, uniform stepwise promotion was feared too lax, and talent was again to be weighed case by case.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王大安元年，定文資本職出身內，有至一品職事官應遷一品散官者，實曆五十月方許告遷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an under Emperor Weishao, within civil-track original functional entry, those reaching first-rank functional office who should transfer to first-rank honorary office required fifty actual months before petitioning for transfer.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an 1 (1209) under Emperor Weishao, civil-track officials who reached first-rank functional posts and sought first-rank honorary rank required fifty actual months before petitioning.

sentences.zh: 二品三品職事官應告本品循遷者，亦曆五十月，不得過本品外。

translations.literal: Second- and third-rank functional officials petitioning for routine transfer within their rank also required fifty months and might not exceed their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Second- and third-rank functional officials seeking routine transfer within their rank also needed fifty months and could not advance beyond their rank.

sentences.zh: 四品以下職事官如遷三品者，亦曆五十月，止許告遷三品一資。

translations.literal: Functional officials of the fourth rank and below transferring to third rank also required fifty months and were permitted to petition for transfer only one grade step within the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank functional officials and below seeking third rank also needed fifty months and could petition for only one grade step within the third rank.

sentences.zh: 六品以下職事官曆六十月告遷，帶至三品更不許告。

translations.literal: Functional officials of the sixth rank and below petitioned for transfer after sixty months; once bearing up to third rank, petition was no longer permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth-rank functional officials and below petitioned after sixty months; once they held third-rank honorary rank, further petitions were barred.

sentences.zh: 犯選格者皆不許。

translations.literal: Those who violated selection regulations were all barred.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had violated selection regulations were barred.

sentences.zh: 如已至三品以上職事者，六十月亦聽。

translations.literal: If already reaching third-rank functional office and above, sixty months was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those already in third-rank functional posts or above were also allowed to petition after sixty months.

sentences.zh: 凡遷三品官資及致仕並橫遷三品者，則具行止以聞。

translations.literal: For all transfers to third-rank official seniority, retirement, and lateral transfers to third rank, conduct records were to be submitted and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Transfers to third-rank seniority, retirement, and lateral transfers to the third rank all required submission of conduct records.

sentences.zh: 四品則六十月告遷，雜班則否。

translations.literal: Fourth rank petitioned for transfer after sixty months; miscellaneous ranks did not.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank officials petitioned after sixty months; miscellaneous ranks did not.

sentences.zh: 宣宗興定元年，徒單頑僧言：「兵興以來，恩命數出，以勞進階者比年尤多。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding under Emperor Xuanzong, Toudan Wanseng said: "Since warfare arose, grace appointments have issued repeatedly; those advanced for merit in recent years are especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 1 (1217) under Emperor Xuanzong, Toudan Wanseng said, "Since the wars began, grace appointments have multiplied, and merit promotions in recent years are especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 賤職下僚散官或至極品，名器之輕莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Low posts and minor subordinates' honorary offices sometimes reach the highest grades—the debasement of titles and offices has never been worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: Men in humble posts sometimes reach the highest honorary ranks—never has the devaluation of office titles been worse.

sentences.zh: 自今非親王子及職一品，餘人雖散官至一品乞皆不許封公。

translations.literal: From now on, except imperial princes and first-rank functional officials, all others though honorary rank reaches first rank beg that enfeoffment as duke not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, except imperial princes and first-rank functional officials, no one should be enfeoffed as duke even if honorary rank reached the first grade.

sentences.zh: 若已封者，雖不追奪其儀衛，亦當降從二品之制。

translations.literal: If already enfeoffed, though their ceremonial guards are not reclaimed, they should still be reduced to secondary second-rank regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Those already enfeoffed, though not stripped of ceremonial guards, should be reduced to secondary second-rank protocol.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The court] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 凡選監察御史，尚書省具才能者疏名進呈，以聽制授。

translations.literal: For selection of censorial investigators, the provincial office listed capable men by name in a memorial and submitted for imperial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial investigators were chosen when the provincial office memorialized capable men by name for imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 任滿，御史台奏其能否，仍視其所察公事具書于解由，以送尚書省。

translations.literal: On term completion, the Censorate memorialized their competence, still viewing the public affairs they investigated and writing them fully in the discharge certificate to send to the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: On term completion the Censorate reported their competence and recorded the cases they had investigated in the discharge certificate sent to the provincial office.

sentences.zh: 如所察事皆無謬戾為稱職，則有升擢。

translations.literal: If all investigated matters were without error and contradiction, deemed competent, then there was promotion.
translations.idiomatic: If their investigations were free of error, they were deemed competent and promoted.

sentences.zh: 庸常者臨期取旨，不稱者降除，任未滿者不許改除。

translations.literal: Mediocre men received instructions at term's end; the unfit were demoted or dismissed; those whose terms were not complete were not permitted changed dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre performers awaited imperial decision at term's end; the unfit were demoted or dismissed; those whose terms were incomplete could not be reassigned.

sentences.zh: 大定二十七年前，嘗令六十以上者為之。

translations.literal: Before the twenty-seventh year of Dading, those sixty and above had been ordered to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Before Dading 27 (1187), the post had been limited to men sixty and older.

sentences.zh: 後，台官以年老者多廢事為言，乃敕尚書省於六品七品內取六十以下廉幹者備選。

translations.literal: Later, censorial officials said that the elderly mostly neglected affairs, and the provincial office was ordered to select from the sixth and seventh ranks men under sixty who were honest and capable as reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Later censorial officials reported that elderly appointees often neglected their duties, and the provincial office was ordered to select honest, capable men under sixty from the sixth and seventh ranks as reserves.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，令台官得自辟舉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, censorial officials were permitted to recommend men themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, censorial officials were allowed to recommend candidates themselves.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，複命尚書省擬注，每一闕則具三人或五人之名，取旨授之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang, the provincial office was again ordered to draft nominations; for each vacancy list three or five names and receive imperial instruction for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 3 (1192) the provincial office again drafted nominations, listing three or five names per vacancy for imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，敕監察給由必經部而後呈省。

translations.literal: In the third year of Cheng'an, it was decreed that censorial discharge certificates must pass through the ministry before submission to the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 3 (1198) censorial discharge certificates were required to pass through the ministry before reaching the provincial office.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，制以給由具所察事之大小多寡定其優劣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, it was regulated that discharge certificates listing the size and number of matters investigated determined excellence or inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4 (1204) discharge certificates were to list investigated cases by size and number to determine the investigator's rating.

sentences.zh: 八年，定制，事有失糾察者以怠慢治罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, a standing rule was fixed: those who failed to investigate and correct matters were punished for negligence.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year a rule fixed that failure to investigate and correct cases was punished as negligence.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，定制以所察大事至五、小事至十為稱職，數不及且無切務者為庸常，數內有二事不實者為不稱職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, a standing rule was fixed: five major matters or ten minor matters investigated counted as competent; numbers not reached and no urgent affairs counted as mediocre; two matters within the count not factual counted as incompetent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 (1214) a rule fixed that five major cases or ten minor cases made an investigator competent; fewer cases with no urgent matters meant mediocrity; two false cases within the count meant incompetence.

sentences.zh: 四年，命台官辟舉，以名申省，定其可否。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, censorial officials were ordered to recommend men, report names to the provincial office, and determine acceptability.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year censorial officials recommended candidates by name to the provincial office for approval.

sentences.zh: 廉察之制，始見於海陵時，故正隆二年六月有廉能官複與差除之令。

translations.literal: The honest-inspection system first appeared under Emperor Hailing; hence in the sixth month of the second year of Zhenglong there was an order again to assign honest and capable officials.
translations.idiomatic: The honest-inspection system first appeared under Emperor Hailing; hence the Zhenglong 2 (1157) order to reassign honest and capable officials.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，命廉到廉能官第一等進官一階升一等，其次約量注授。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading, honest investigators arriving found first-grade honest and capable officials promoted one rank step and one grade; the rest received approximate draft appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 3 (1163) first-grade honest and capable officials found by inspectors were promoted one rank step and one grade; others received appropriate draft appointments.

sentences.zh: 汙濫官第一等殿三年降二等，次二年，又次一年，皆降一等。

translations.literal: Corrupt officials first grade: detained three years and demoted two grades; second grade two years; third grade one year—all demoted one grade.
translations.idiomatic: First-grade corrupt officials were detained three years and demoted two grades; second-grade two years and one grade down; third-grade one year and one grade down.

sentences.zh: 詔廉問猛安謀克，廉能者第一等遷兩官，其次遷一官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered honest inquiry of meng'an and mouke; honest and capable first grade transferred two offices; the next transferred one office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered honest inspection of meng'an and mouke units; first-grade honest and capable leaders advanced two offices, the next grade one office.

sentences.zh: 汙濫者第一等決杖百，罷去，擇其兄弟代之。

translations.literal: Corrupt first grade: sentenced to one hundred strokes, dismissed, and a brother chosen to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: First-grade corrupt leaders were sentenced to one hundred strokes, dismissed, and replaced by a brother.

sentences.zh: 第二等杖八十，第三等杖七十，皆令複職。

translations.literal: Second grade eighty strokes, third grade seventy strokes—all ordered to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Second-grade offenders received eighty strokes and third-grade seventy, and all were ordered back to office.

sentences.zh: 蒲輦決則罷去，永不補差。

translations.literal: If the council decided, then dismissed, never again supplemented or assigned.
translations.idiomatic: If the council ruled against them, they were dismissed and never reassigned.

sentences.zh: 八年，省臣奏御史中丞移剌道所廉之官，上曰：「職官多貪污，以致罪廢，其餘亦有因循以苟歲月者。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, provincial ministers memorialized the officials investigated by Censor-in-Chief Yila Dao; the emperor said: "Functional officials are mostly corrupt, leading to crime and dismissal; the rest also drift along to get through the months.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year provincial ministers reported the officials investigated by Censor-in-Chief Yila Dao. The emperor said, "Most officials are corrupt and end up dismissed for crimes; the rest merely coast through their terms.

sentences.zh: 今所察能實可甄獎，若即與升除，恐無以慰民愛留之意，且可遷加，候秩滿日升除。

translations.literal: Those now investigated as truly able may be selected for reward; if immediately promoted or dismissed, I fear there is no way to satisfy the people's wish to retain them—for now they may be transferred and advanced, waiting until rank completion day for promotion or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Those found truly capable deserve reward, but immediate promotion might disappoint the people who wish to keep them. For now they may receive rank advancement and promotion or dismissal when their terms end.

sentences.zh: 」十年正月，上謂宰臣曰：「今天下州縣之職多闕員，朕欲不限資歷用人，何以遍知其能。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the tenth year, the emperor told the chief ministers: "Today prefectural and county posts throughout the empire mostly lack incumbents. I wish to employ men without limiting seniority—how can I know their abilities everywhere?
translations.idiomatic: " In the first month of the tenth year the emperor told his chief ministers, "Prefectural and county posts stand vacant across the empire. I wish to appoint without seniority limits—how can I know every man's ability?

sentences.zh: 擬欲遣使廉問，又慮擾民而未得其真。

translations.literal: I plan to send envoys for honest inquiry, yet also fear disturbing the people and not obtaining the truth.
translations.idiomatic: I consider sending envoys for honest inspection, yet fear disturbing the people and still not learning the truth.

sentences.zh: 若令行辟舉之法，複恐久則生弊。

translations.literal: If the method of recommendation is implemented, I again fear that in time abuses will arise.
translations.idiomatic: If we rely on recommendation, I fear abuses will arise over time.

sentences.zh: 不若選人暗察明廉，如其相同，然後升黜之，何如？

translations.literal: Better to have selected men investigate secretly and inquire openly; if they match, then promote or demote—how would that be?
translations.idiomatic: Better to have selected men investigate secretly and inquire openly, and promote or demote when the results match—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」宰臣曰：「當如聖訓。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers said: "It should follow the sage instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers said, "We shall follow Your Majesty's instruction.

sentences.zh: 」十一年，奏所廉善惡官，上曰：「罪重者遣官就治，所犯細微者蓋不能禁制妻拏耳，其誡勵而釋之。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh year, good and bad officials from honest inspection were memorialized; the emperor said: "For heavy crimes send officials to punish on the spot; for slight offenses they probably could not restrain wives and children—admonish and release them.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh year good and bad officials from inspection were reported. The emperor said, "Send officials to punish serious crimes on the spot; for minor offenses they probably could not control their households—admonish and release them.

sentences.zh: 凡廉能官，四品以下委官覆實，同則升擢。

translations.literal: For all honest and capable officials of the fourth rank and below, commission officials to verify; if matching, then promote.
translations.idiomatic: Honest and capable officials of the fourth rank and below were to be verified by commissioned officials and promoted if confirmed.

sentences.zh: 三品以上以聞，朕自處之。

translations.literal: Third rank and above report to me; I will handle them myself.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above were to be reported to me for my own decision.

sentences.zh: 」時陳言者有雲：「每三年委宰執一員廉問者。

translations.literal: " At that time some who submitted memorials said: "Every three years commission one chief minister for honest inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: " Some memorialists suggested commissioning one chief minister every three years for honest inspection.

sentences.zh: 」上以大臣出則郡縣動搖，誰複敢行事者。

translations.literal: " The emperor said that when great ministers go out, prefectures and counties are shaken—who would again dare to conduct affairs?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied that when great ministers tour the circuits, prefectures and counties are thrown into turmoil and no one dares govern normally.

sentences.zh: 今默察明問之制，蓋得其中矣。

translations.literal: Today's system of secret investigation and open inquiry probably hits the mean.
translations.idiomatic: The present system of secret investigation and open inquiry strikes the right balance.

sentences.zh: 又謂宰臣曰：「朕以欲遍知天下官吏善惡，故每使採訪，其被升黜者多矣，宜知勸也。

translations.literal: He again told the chief ministers: "Because I wish to know the good and bad of officials throughout the empire, I constantly send investigators; many have been promoted or demoted—they should know encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He again told his chief ministers, "Because I wish to know the character of officials everywhere, I constantly send investigators. Many have been promoted or demoted—they should take the hint.

sentences.zh: 若常設訪察，恐任非其人以之生弊，是以姑罷之。

translations.literal: If investigation were permanently established, I fear the wrong men would be assigned and abuses would arise—therefore for now it is suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Permanent investigators might be the wrong men and breed abuses, so for now the system is suspended.

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「是官不設，何以知官吏之善惡也？

translations.literal: " All said: "If this office is not established, how can we know officials' good and bad?
translations.idiomatic: " All said, "Without such an office, how can we know which officials are good or bad?

sentences.zh: 」左丞相良弼曰：「自今臣等盡心親察之。

translations.literal: " Left Chancellor Liang Bi said: "From now on we your subjects will give our full hearts to investigate personally.
translations.idiomatic: " Left Chancellor Liang Bi said, "From now on we shall investigate personally with all our effort.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「宜加詳，勿使名實淆混。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "You should add detail and not let name and reality become confused.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Be thorough and do not confuse reputation with reality.

sentences.zh: 」十二年，以同知城陽軍山和尚等清強，上曰：「此輩，暗察明訪皆著政聲。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth year, because Vice Commissioner of Chengyang Army Shan Heshang and others were honest and forceful, the emperor said: "These men—secret investigation and open inquiry both record outstanding administrative reputations.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth year, because Chengyang Army Vice Commissioner Shan Heshang and others were honest and forceful, the emperor said, "These men earned outstanding reputations in both secret investigation and open inquiry.

sentences.zh: 夫賞罰必信，則善者勸、惡者懼，此道久行庶可得人也。

translations.literal: When rewards and punishments are sure to be trusted, the good are encouraged and the bad fear—if this way is long practiced, perhaps worthy men can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards and punishments are reliable, the good are encouraged and the bad fear. If this practice continues, worthy men may be found.

sentences.zh: 其第其政績旌賞之。

translations.literal: Grade their administrative achievements and commend and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: Grade their administrative achievements and reward them.

sentences.zh: 」三月，詔贓官既已被廉，若仍舊在職必複害民，其遣驛使遍詣諸道，即日罷之。

translations.literal: " In the third month, an edict [stated that] corrupt officials who have already been investigated, if still in office will again harm the people—dispatch courier envoys throughout the circuits and dismiss them the same day.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month an edict ruled that corrupt officials already exposed by inspection, if left in office, would harm the people again; courier envoys were sent to every circuit to dismiss them immediately.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年，制以閣門祗候、筆硯承奏、奉職、妃護衛，東宮入殿小底，宗室郎君，王府郎君、省郎君，始以選試才能用之，不須體察。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Dading, it was regulated that gate attendants, brush-and-ink memorial presenters, ceremonial attendants, consort guards, Eastern Palace inner-hall attendants, imperial clan gentlemen, princely household gentlemen, and provincial gentlemen were first selected by testing ability for use, without investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 28 (1188) gate attendants, memorial presenters, ceremonial attendants, consort guards, Eastern Palace attendants, imperial clan gentlemen, princely household gentlemen, and provincial gentlemen were first chosen by ability tests without investigation.

sentences.zh: 內藏本把、不入殿小底、與入殿小底、及知把書畫，則亦不體察。

translations.literal: Inner-storehouse custodians, non-hall attendants, hall attendants, and custodians of calligraphy and painting were also not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-storehouse custodians, non-hall and hall attendants, and custodians of calligraphy and painting were likewise exempt from investigation.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，以所廉察則有清廉之聲，而政績則平常者，敕命不降注。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang, those investigated as having a reputation for honesty and cleanness but ordinary administrative achievements were ordered not to receive demoted draft nomination.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 3 (1192) officials with reputations for honesty but only ordinary achievements were ordered not to receive demoted nominations.

sentences.zh: 以石仲淵等四人，雖清廉為百姓所喜，而複有行事邀順人情之語，則與公正廉能人不同，敕命降注。

translations.literal: Because Shi Zhongyuan and four others, though honest and clean and pleasing to the common people, also had conduct of courting popular sentiment in their words, they differed from fair, upright, honest, and capable men—an edict ordered demoted draft nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhongyuan and four others, though honest and popular with the people, had been reported as courting popular sentiment in their conduct and differed from truly upright officials; they received demoted nominations.

sentences.zh: 凡治績平常者，奪元舉官俸一月。

translations.literal: For all with ordinary administrative achievements, strip the original recommender's salary for one month.
translations.idiomatic: For ordinary administrative performance, the original recommender's salary was withheld for one month.

sentences.zh: 四年，上曰：「凡被舉者，或先選者不同，其後為人再舉而察者同，或先察者同，而後察者不同，當何以處之？

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the emperor said: "For all who are recommended, sometimes the first selection differs, and later when others recommend again the investigation matches; or the first investigation matches and the later investigation differs—how should this be handled?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor said, "When a recommended official's first selection differs from a later recommendation that investigation confirms, or early investigation matches but later investigation differs, how should we proceed?

sentences.zh: 其議可久通行無窒之術以聞。

translations.literal: Discuss methods that can be long practiced without obstruction and report.
translations.idiomatic: Discuss methods that can be applied long term without obstruction and report.

sentences.zh: 」省臣奏曰：「保舉與體察不一者，可除不相攝提刑司境內職事，再令體察，如果同則依格用，不同則還本資歷。

translations.literal: " Provincial ministers reported: "Where recommendation and investigation disagree, dismiss from functional posts within non-overlapping Punishments Bureau jurisdictions, investigate again; if matching then employ according to regulations, if different then return to original seniority.
